newsitem.title: UK: CWC denies report of investment cutbacks.
newsitem.headline: CWC denies report of investment cutbacks.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Communications Plc, Britain's biggest telephone and cable television company, on Wednesday denied that it had any plans to cut back investments or capital expenditure.
The Independent newspaper reported the company had failed to meet profit targets set by its parent, Cable and Wireless Plc, and had been forced to rein in investment plans.
"There are absolutely no proposals to cut capital expenditure," a company spokeswoman told Reuters.
She also dismissed as "totally absurd" the newspaper's allegation there were tensions between C&W's chief executive Richard Brown and Graham Wallace, his counterpart at CWC.

Andrew Moffat, telecoms analyst at SocGen, said he had been told CWC's plans to invest 2.2-2.4 billion pounds over the next two years were on target and the group's plans to launch digital television were also on schedule. However, Moffat expects any small downturn in revenue to be made up within the year.

The company has said it was ready to launch the multi-channel service in the Autumn but was likely to wait until early next year until a similar offering is launched by British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc.
CWC, which is majority-owned by C&W, was launched after a four-way merger between telephone carrier Mercury and three cable television companies in April.
